thread:
ana: Heads-up — planning a rollout for stricter fncall schema validation next week. Want to align on what we expose in the Console dashboard and what telemetry we ship.

devon: +1. Do you mean strict reject vs soft-validate?

ana: yeah. Two parts: (1) counters for rejects vs coerces, with reason-code tags; (2) a per-route sampling of payloads (redacted) for debugging. Also need routing fallback counts (when requests switch to degen/backup model).

mike: For counters, can we reuse existing metric names? `fncall.rejects`, `fncall.coerces`? add `reason` tag like `schema_mismatch`, `missing_field`, `type_error`?

lina: That works. Need to be careful about cardinality — reason is fine, but don't tag with full param names. Also add `route_id` and `model_variant` tags.

devon: Sampling: suggest 0.1% by default, adjustable per-org. Store sample payloads in a secure bucket with redaction pipeline. We'll need opt-out for regulated customers.

ana: Agree on sampling rate. For dashboard UX: show a small heatmap of recent reject spikes per-route and a drilldown with sampled payloads + trace id. Also a toggle to view only billed vs non-billed rejects.

mike: Question: do we bill rejected fncalls? Current billing counts token decode attempts even if we later reject. Product said we shouldn't surprise customers.

lina: Product asked for transparency: show a metric `fncall.billing_impact` that estimates billed tokens from rejected calls. Not sure about changing billing behavior now.

devon: Technical note: our sampler needs to attach `trace.id` to metric so drilldown links to traces. Add `trace_id` tag on sample events.

ana: Also want a routing metric `fncall.fallback.count` with tag `fallback_reason` (e.g., `overload`, `strict_reject`, `region_unavail`). That'll help Ops tune autoscale vs permissive rollback.

sre-bot: Incident note: last canary had a spike in `fallback_reason=strict_reject` after we bumped strictness to 50% — ops paged twice.

mike: Oof. So rollout plan: start strict validation at 1% with quick ramp if no spike in rejects > 0.5% of traffic for 24h. Also expose a per-customer quick rollback toggle in Console.

lina: For telemetry retention, we should keep aggregates for 90 days, samples for 30 days by default. Make retention configurable.

devon: Quick schema for metric tags proposal (pseudo):
```
metric: fncall.rejects
tags: [route_id, model_variant, reason]

metric: fncall.fallback.count
tags: [route_id, fallback_reason, target_model]
```

mike: Implementation detail: validators run in the router layer; we can emit the metrics there before handing to model. Need to ensure low overhead — counters + asynchronous sample enqueue only when sample hit.

ana: UX text: Console should show explanation copy: "Rejects indicate structured output didn't match the declared schema. Learn how to soften validation or add perms for your route." Link to docs.

devon: Docs + SDK: add client-side validation helper and example for `soft_validate: true` flag in request. Sample code block for server-side telemetry is needed.

lina: Security: sampled payloads must be scanned and PII redacted. Use existing redaction lib; add unit tests for edgecases (credit card, SSN).

mike: Action items: (1) Devon to add metric emit + sampler PR, (2) Lina to draft dashboard tiles and retention knobs, (3) Ana to write rollout checklist + Console toggle copy, (4) SRE to author runbook for sudden reject spikes.

ana: I'll file a rollout RFC and ping infra for a canary window. Thanks all. :+1:

devon: I'll start a spike on the sampler this afternoon.

mike: I'll do the runbook skeleton and post link.

lina: Drafting dashboard mock now, will post screenshot in thread.

sre-bot: Deploy reminder: canary window scheduled Tue 09:00-12:00 UTC.
